title: Desk Guidance — Statement Lead Time for Recently Posted Encounter Lines, Patient Financial Account
content:
How lines of the most recent encounter are carried on a pre-placement statement of the Patient Financial Account depends on the account:

- for an account whose tier requires a card on file and that holds one, a line posted fewer than the tier's card-on-file advance-notice days (5 calendar days on the High-Deductible Health Plan Account) before the handling date that carries no card-on-file payment is left off for the next cycle;
- for any other account whose statement delivery channel is mail, a line posted fewer than 3 calendar days before the handling date is left off for the next cycle;
- for any other account, no line is left off under this guidance.

The open part of each line left off is what is left off.

## Terms used

- **Most recent encounter** — for the pre-placement statement, the encounter whose deductible or coinsurance line was posted last.
- **Its lines** — its deductible line, its coinsurance line and its non-covered service line.
- **Open part of a line** — its amount less the payments posted against that line.
- **Card-on-file payment on a line** — a payment posted against that line and received through the card on file.
- **Holds a card on file** — the account record shows a card on file; "the tier requires a card on file" is the class's card-on-file terms (the High-Deductible Health Plan Account is the class that requires one).

## Points of judgement

| Tier requires a card on file and account holds one | Statement channel | Line posted | Card-on-file payment on the line | Line's open part left off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | any | fewer than 5 days ago | none | yes |
| yes | any | fewer than 5 days ago | yes | no |
| yes | any | 5 or more days ago | any | no |
| no | mail | fewer than 3 days ago | — | yes |
| no | mail | 3 or more days ago | — | no |
| no | paperless | any | — | no |

The first three rows apply whatever the channel: an account that requires and holds a card on file is judged on the advance-notice days even when its statements go by mail.

## Worked case (hypothetical figures)

A mail account on a class with no card-on-file requirement; handling date day 10. The most recent encounter has a deductible line of 300.00 posted on day 8 with 50.00 paid against it, a coinsurance line of 90.00 posted on day 4, and no non-covered service line. The deductible line was posted 2 days ago, fewer than 3, so its open part of 250.00 is left off; the coinsurance line, posted 6 days ago, is not.
